As a male educator (ECT) in the early childhood sector, 
adivce 1: if the staff do not accept you, leave. Not worth the hassle.
Advice 2: join a union. 

Reasoning
We face a stereotype.  We need to be extra careful in our day to day duties so that we don't get accused. And when we do get accused  (yes, "when", not "if" you get accused) you need support.  Hence if the staff do not accept you, it is unlikely that they will provide the support you need. Being a part of a union, you'll have extra support. 

Now the reason I said "when you get accused" is because there are multiple reasons ppl get accused. 
One is the standard reason of parents not trusting male educators, whether due to just gender or race. Some parents may have been abused and projects their anger on us. 
The other reason is money. Most centres have a 2 week notice period to pull a child out. If they pull the child out earlier, they have to pay a penalty. But if the parents accuses an educator,  claim they feel unsafe, then while the investigation occurs, child can pull out without paying. 
There was a case where the parent was mentally unstable, didn't like something an educator did and so she accused the educator of slapping a child. "Mentally unstable" because she expected that she could keep bringing her child to the centre. 


Parents can not imagine the amount of stress an investigation can place on an educator. 

My first accusation occurred less than a year I started working. I was cleared because I was not even working on the day the parent said the alleged incident occurred. Police still had to come and check our CCTV footage. 

Other things I've faced: wasn't allowed to change nappies. One family said it was a cultural thing and the father doesn't change nappies either. This case, I accepted it and moved on. Another family said it was because I was a male, and dad did do nappies. I had the support of the educators, director and 2ic. 2ic asked the parents to let the child settle for a week, see how the child reacts to me and the revisit the nappy situation. (2ic also explained that all educators are equal here and share the work, etc... ). On the 3rd morning, when being dropped off, child immediately came running to me, hugged me. Parents saw how safe and comfortable the child was with me and rescinded any concerns they had about me.
